Description: Larkin Street Youth Services (Larkin Street) is the San Francisco Bay Area’s largest nonprofit provider of housing and services for youth experiencing homelessness, serving transition-age youth (TAY) across housing, wellness, education, and employment domains. Larkin Street’s wraparound approach to ending youth homelessness combines outreach and engagement services (including a mobile street outreach team, two neighborhood drop-in centers, and two emergency shelters) with a continuum of housing interventions (transitional, supportive, and subsidy-based), as well as case management, primary and behavioral health care, education, and employment support. Larkin Street approaches service delivery from a set of best practices employed specifically to reduce barriers, promote resilience, and center each participant’s well-being. These evidence-based practices include Housing First, Harm Reduction, Trauma Informed Care, Non-Violent Crisis Intervention, Restorative Practices, and Positive Youth Development.

Description: I am a therapist, moving into this building with other therapists and lawyers. My original application was denied, however, it is unclear to me how other therapists rent in this building. When looking on the berkeley municipal code website, under the Elmwood business improvement district, under 7.84.010, it lists: "Professional Businesses" include those providing services that require a high degree deal of training or expertise, Berkeley Business License Tax Code P. Examples include attorneys, architects, accountants, engineers, surveyors, therapists and others in a medical/health service field, consultants, real estate brokers, financial advisors, artists and designers.
